teacher_walkthrough:
Write down the given probability mass formula for the random variable $X$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = x) = k x^2$$

Evaluate the probability for $x = -2$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = -2) = k(-2)^2 = k(4) = 4k$$

Evaluate the probability for $x = 2$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = 2) = k(2)^2 = k(4) = 4k$$

Since $(-2)^2 = 2^2 = 4$, both expressions yield the exact same value $4k$:
$$\mathrm{P}(X = -2) = \mathrm{P}(X = 2) = 4k$$

Set up the probability distribution table displaying the values of $x$ and their corresponding probabilities in terms of $k$.
Recall that the sum of all probabilities in a valid distribution must equal 1, and solve for $k$.

Present the probability distribution table for $X$:
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & -2 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & 4k & k & 4k & 16k \\ \hline\end{array}$$

Use the total probability condition $\sum \mathrm{P}(X = x) = 1$ to find $k$:

$$\begin{array}{c|cccc} x & -2 & -1 & 2 & 4 \\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X = x) & 4k & k & 4k & 16k \end{array}$$

$$\sum_{x} \mathrm{P}(X = x) = 1$$

$$4k + k + 4k + 16k = 1$$
$$25k = 1$$
$$k = \frac{1}{25} = 0.04$$
